task: Cooper's read section 5 - is data/daily a market-wide pull or a selected one?
why: A bound built on a selected control set is not a bound. T3 measured breadth and explicitly did not establish provenance; this settles it.
cooper_test: 'the ticker count PER SESSION, distributed. A market-wide daily pull has a stable count near the listed-universe size and moves only with listings and delistings. A selected pull varies with whatever selected it.'

result_1_per_session_count.reading: STABLE, and what movement there is is MONOTONE IN TIME rather than in market activity. CV 1.03% and a +0.891 correlation with the session INDEX is the signature of a roster that grows with net listings. A pull selected on activity would vary with activity - spiky, and correlated with volatility or volume, not with the calendar. So it is NOT activity-selected.

result_2_overlap_with_the_archive._why_this_was_added: The per-session test rules out activity-selection but cannot distinguish a market-wide pull from any other stable roster - including one derived from the archive itself. Ticker overlap settles that, and it changes the answer.
result_2_overlap_with_the_archive.reading: 54.2% of daily/ tickers are absent from the archive entirely - including AAPL, A, AAON. Large caps that a micro-cap momentum archive would never contain. So daily/ is NOT derived from the archive; it is an independent pull. It also contains ETFs (AADR, AAPD), warrants (AAM.WS) and units (AAM.U), so it is not filtered to common stock.

verdict.is_it_activity_selected: NO - CV 1.03%, drift monotone in time not activity.
verdict.is_it_derived_from_the_archive: NO - 54.2% of its tickers are absent from the archive.
verdict.is_it_market_wide: NO. 1,836 tickers is well below the US listed common-stock universe, and it mixes instrument types. It is a stable, independent, BROAD roster - but not the market.
verdict.is_it_fit_for_the_control_set_purpose: NO, AND THIS IS THE DECIDING NUMBER: it holds only 216 of the 904 archive tickers in its own window. 688 are missing - 76.1%. A resource meant to bound how often a screen fires on names the archive does not contain cannot do so while omitting three quarters of the names the archive DOES contain in the same window.

consequence_for_route_R4: R4 in routes_and_costs.json was conditioned on data/daily being establishable as a market-wide set. It is not. R4 as written does not produce a bound. What it could still produce is a statement about a stable 1,836-name roster over four months, which is a different and much weaker object, and the routes table should be read with that correction.
cost: minutes, as predicted. Two duckdb queries plus a set comparison.
